+WINNER: transition_branch_hyperbolic_prototypes
+FIRST LISTED: transition_branch_hyperbolic_prototypes
+ARGUMENT: behavior_evidence and downstream_mechanism: A directly models each item's successor branches and names prefix transition predictability as a diagnostic tied to improved Stage 3 Recall@10; the shared ledger shows that nearby directed-assignment/prefix mechanisms are mixed or negative (E14, E16-E21), making this a specific, testable behavioral route rather than a generic prior. B's interest-mixture signal is plausible but has no measured support in this evidence bundle (its E1-E3 are proposed). novelty/exploration_value: A is a distinct successor-distribution prototype computation, whereas B layers user mixtures with balanced assignment, resembling the ledger's capacity-balanced/constrained assignment attempts, both below baseline (E17-E18). Neither has checked prior art (E9), but A is the more informative first experiment. implementability: A specifies sparse training-only preprocessing and minibatch prototype scoring, estimated at 10-30% overhead; B's Sinkhorn and compatibility path is less concretely costed and its stated full recomputation cost is substantial. The ledger's observed geometry/transition variants span 0.05557-0.06375 (E11-E22), so neither has evidence of reaching the 0.065 target.
+FAILURE RISK: A may be wrong if sparse/noisy successor histories or popularity-dominated branches make q_i uninformative, or if the Lorentz prototype term adds no value over a matched Euclidean control; the ledger's weak/negative directed and hyperbolic results (E14, E19-E22) make this a material risk.
*** End Patch

part.text:
WINNER: transition_branch_hyperbolic_prototypes
FIRST LISTED: transition_branch_hyperbolic_prototypes
ARGUMENT: behavior_evidence and downstream_mechanism: A directly models each item’s successor branches and names prefix transition predictability as a diagnostic tied to improved Stage 3 Recall@10. The ledger shows nearby directed-assignment and prefix mechanisms have mixed or negative results (E14, E16–E21), making A a specific, testable behavioral route rather than a generic prior. B’s interest-mixture signal is plausible but has no measured support in this bundle (its E1–E3 are proposed). novelty/exploration_value: A proposes a distinct successor-distribution prototype computation, whereas B combines user mixtures with balanced assignment, close to capacity-balanced/constrained assignment attempts that fell below baseline (E17–E18). Neither has checked prior art (E9), but A is the more informative first experiment. implementability: A specifies sparse training-only preprocessing and minibatch prototype scoring, estimated at 10–30% overhead. B’s Sinkhorn and compatibility path is less concretely costed, and its stated full-recomputation cost is substantial. The observed geometry/transition variants span 0.05557–0.06375 (E11–E22), so neither is demonstrated to reach the 0.065 target.
FAILURE RISK: A may be wrong if sparse or noisy successor histories, popularity-dominated branches, or the Lorentz prototype term make its signal uninformative—or if it adds no value over a matched Euclidean control. The weak or negative directed and hyperbolic results in the ledger (E14, E19–E22) make this a material risk.
